absent: Shard range table allocation, publication, resizing and RCU reclamation lifecycle.
Allocation sizing macro and maximum supported CPU identity count.
Full dispatch queue object layout, identifier allocation and lock ordering.
Scheduler enable, disable, watchdog recovery and bypass activation sequences.
Contents and calling contexts of the registered BPF helper sets.
Complete task iterator object layout and cgroup mode locking rules.
Exit code and CPU selection policy and downstream disable work actions.
Virtual time and slice handling during dispatch queue iteration.
Direct dispatch task lifecycle and kick synchronization protocol.
Dump output format and trace point payload definitions.

findings.text: The shard extraction routine publishes the portion of a referenced CPU identity mask that overlaps a given shard into a caller supplied mask object, anchoring empty results at the shard start.

Two helpers fold a concrete mask into the storage behind a mask reference, one merging set bits and the other replacing the overlapped region, both delegating the ranged walk to a shared two operand walker.
The CID kfunc initialization entry attempts registration of the CID helper sets across complementary BPF program categories in sequence, succeeding only if each step succeeds.

A formatted exit entry accepts a scheduler, exit classification, code, CPU and message template plus arguments, forwards them through a variadic completer, and reports whether this caller won the exit claim.

Ancestry is tested by level comparison plus ancestor table slot equality, while node local and user dispatch queues are resolved by NUMA node index and by hash lookup on queue identifier respectively.
A small iterator API opens, temporarily releases, reacquires and closes traversal over scheduler tasks, supporting both a global list mode and a cgroup descendant mode.

Membership holds exactly when an identifier lies inside half open range from base for the stated count, and the storage word is derived from the difference of sixty four sized block indices between identifier and base.
Initialization clamps the requested count down to the allocated capacity when undersized, records base and count and capacity in words, and clears the whole allocated storage.

Reframing refuses to change anything when the new span needs more words than allocated, otherwise it clears edge storage and updates base and count; set and test silently ignore identifiers outside the current span.

Empty masks report zero used words, otherwise the count covers the bit offset of base plus length; iteration walks used words in order, yielding only set positions observed through single reads and bit scans.

Forward list traversal starts from the queue head or a given task and steps in the chosen direction until the head repeats, skipping markers reserved for active BPF iteration cursors and returning only real tasks.
Negative inputs and non CID operation pass through unchanged, otherwise the value is translated from CID to CPU through the scheduler context.
Only three reserved dispatch queue identities are considered owned by the run queue; all other identifiers are treated as not run queue owned.
Two unsigned thirty two bit sequence values are ordered by interpreting their difference as signed, so later values remain greater across wrap.
Stop tasks keep the stop class while others resolve through policy and priority; bypass enqueue climbs past bypassing ancestors toward the nearest non bypassing scheduler or root.
Non local dispatch queue traversal and cursor advance require the queue lock held, enforced by assertion at entry.
Run queue openness checks, queue loss checks, locked run queue tracking updates, and run queue switching assume the relevant run queue lock is already held.

Global task iteration acquires a dedicated task list lock around list membership, while scheduler hash and task hash document insertion under dedicated scheduler and task locks with elastic hash behavior.
The variadic exit path holds a preemption guard around the claim, and the abort sweep traverses descendants under a read side guard while marking each node aborting before walking its children.

The CID tables aggregate a shard count plus per CPU mappings between CPU and CID and shard and node, plus per shard range descriptors and topology descriptors, ending with a deferred reclamation header.
Kick synchronization state pairs a reclamation header with a trailing variable length array and is kept as a per CPU RCU pointer; task identifier allocation keeps per CPU next and end cursors.

Dump state records target CPU, first flag, cursor, output buffer pointer, prefix and scratch string buffer; the kernel BPF dispatch iterator holds a list cursor plus queue pointer and slice and virtual time, mirrored by an opaque fixed size user view with shared alignment.

Three hash tables are keyed respectively by sub cgroup identifier, by task identifier, and by dispatch queue identifier, each recording key length and offsets for key and hash node within the owning object.
Dispatch iteration flags distinguish one user visible reverse bit from two internal presence bits for slice and virtual time, with combined masks for user only and for all valid bits.

Exit proceeds from none to a concrete kind exactly once; parent exits only mark the local abort flag while other kinds abort the whole subtree, emit a trace, record message and metadata, then queue disable work.

Openness is decided by class ordering relative to the extension class, then by dispatch nesting, then by preempt flag with protected slice veto, otherwise closed when an extension task occupies the run queue.

Cursor advance skips entries queued after cursor creation by sequence comparison, repositions the cursor beside the returned task in the direction of travel, or detaches it at end; a task is deemed lost on queue mismatch or newer sequence or held CPU or run queue mismatch.

Start clears state then either walks cgroup descendants with dead tasks included or inserts a list cursor under lock; unlock releases run queue then list, relock reacquires in opposite order, and stop removes the cursor and releases all locks.
Module initialization registers CID helpers for several BPF contexts, while slice and load balance interval parameters expose custom setters with clamped ranges and standard unsigned getters.
If the caller destination cannot hold the overlapped words, an error is logged and the result is forced empty at the shard base rather than truncating.
Backtrace capture is skipped when exiting from non maskable interrupt context, and the abort sweep uses lockless ordered marks plus deferred work so recovery cannot be delayed by callbacks.
Undersized allocation during init truncates the usable count, and oversized reframe requests leave the existing base and count untouched, both guarded by warnings.

The module parameter prefix fact is sched_ext with trailing dot, and the CID header uses a conventional include guard macro; trace points are enabled by defining a creation macro in the extension core.
The reverse iteration option occupies bit sixteen, while internal slice present and virtual time present indicators occupy bits thirty and thirty one.

Slice bypass accepts one hundred through one hundred thousand microseconds, bypass interval accepts zero through ten million microseconds; task identifier cursor starts at one while scheduler identifier cursor, enable sequence and rejection and hotplug counters start at zero, and dump CPU starts at negative one.

At load the extension reports disabled and unswitched with task translation off and non CID identity mode, with plain flags for initial task handling and global switching clear, and the enabling sub scheduler slot is either a writable pointer or a null constant depending on build selection.

The extension keeps a global RCU scheduler root, a hash of schedulers, a task hash, an enable mutex, enablement static keys, cgroup flag, rejection and hotplug and enable sequence counters, and identifier cursors for tasks and schedulers.

Watchdog state pairs an interval with a timestamp initialized to the initial jiffies value plus delayed work; dump state defaults to no CPU; a kset pointer and slice bypass and load balance interval tunables complete the control block.
Locked run queue and direct dispatch task are maintained per CPU with small helpers to read and update the locked pointer under assertion that the target is held.
Run queue lock handover clears tracking if the source was tracked, drops and acquires the underlying spin locks in order, then restores tracking to the destination when applicable.
Each exit kind maps to a distinct human phrase covering unregister sources and parent causes and error subclasses, with unrecognized kinds yielding an unknown marker.
